title: This Fish Shoots Insects Out of the Air and Almost Never Misses
subject: archerfish

scenes.text: This fish shoots insects out of the air, and almost never misses.
It spits a jet of water, and the insect falls in. But water bends light.
Looking up through the surface, the insect isn't where it looks. Yet the fish aims right.
Researchers found the fish can hit targets up to about six body lengths away.
And the jet keeps its force. The water merges into one mass just before impact.
One scientist compared the fish's maths to an outfielder judging where a fly ball lands.

description:
The archerfish knocks insects off branches with a jet of water, and it almost never misses.
A study at Wake Forest University found the jet's force barely drops for targets up to six body lengths away.
Could you hit a target through water?
first_comment: Archerfish also pick the closer target when given a choice, so rivals can't steal the meal. Smart or what?
